entries.a:
A few simple habits that work well with Worthwise:
- Wait a day or two before any non-essential purchase.
- Keep your **emergency fund** growing before big buys.
- Keep your monthly expenses below income so your **surplus** stays positive.
- Add a **goal** so you can see what a purchase would delay.

These are general habits, not professional financial advice.
entries.hi:
Kuch aasaan aadatein jo Worthwise ke saath achhi chalti hain:
- Zaroori na ho to kharidne se pehle ek-do din ruk jaiye.
- Bade purchase se pehle **emergency fund** badhaiye.
- Kharche income se kam rakhiye taaki **surplus** positive rahe.
- Ek **goal** add kijiye taaki dikhe ki purchase se kya delay hoga.

Ye general aadatein hain, professional financial advice nahi.

k: how many times can i try
entries.a:
In the **demo / trial account** you can run **2 analyses** (2 requests). A small banner at the top shows how many are left, for example "Demo mode · 1 of 2 analyses left".

Once both are used, the demo is finished. To keep using Worthwise, **create a free account with your real email**: you will get a 6-digit verification code on that email, and your own profile, goals and decisions are then saved under your account.

Tip: tapping **Try Demo** again in the same browser resumes the same demo, it does not give you new analyses.
entries.hi:
**Demo / trial account** mein aap **2 analyses** (2 requests) chala sakte hain. Upar ek chhota banner dikhata hai kitne bache hain, jaise "Demo mode · 1 of 2 analyses left".

Dono khatam hone ke baad demo poora ho jata hai. Worthwise aage use karne ke liye **apni asli (original) email se free account banayein**: us email par 6-digit verification code aayega, aur phir aapka profile, goals aur decisions aapke account mein save rahenge.

Tip: usi browser mein dobara **Try Demo** dabane par wahi purana demo khulta hai, naye analyses nahi milte.
next: How do I create an account?

entries.a:
With a **real account** (created with your original email):
- **Purchase decisions** are always calculated, with **no limit**.
- The **AI explanation** and the **live product search** (Market Research) have a **monthly limit**. The dashboard card **API Usage This Month** shows how many you have used, how many are left and the date they reset.
- Your profile, goals and decisions are saved to your account.

In the **demo** you only get **2 analyses**, so a real account is the way to keep using Worthwise.
entries.hi:
**Real account** (apni original email se banaya hua) mein:
- **Purchase decisions** hamesha calculate hote hain, **koi limit nahi**.
- **AI explanation** aur **live product search** (Market Research) ki **monthly limit** hoti hai. Dashboard ka **API Usage This Month** card dikhata hai kitna use hua, kitna bacha aur kab reset hoga.
- Aapka profile, goals aur decisions aapke account mein save rehte hain.

**Demo** mein sirf **2 analyses** milte hain, isliye aage use karne ke liye real account banana hoga.
next: How do I create an account?

entries.a:
To **delete your account**:
- **Desktop:** click **Delete account** at the bottom of the left sidebar.
- **Mobile:** open the **Account** tab in the bottom bar, then tap **Delete account** at the bottom of the sheet.
- Enter your **password** to confirm.

This **permanently deletes** your account, financial profile, goals and all purchase decisions, and it **cannot be undone**. If you only want to sign out, use **Logout** instead.
entries.hi:
**Account delete** karne ke liye:
- **Desktop:** left sidebar ke neeche **Delete account** par click karein.
- **Mobile:** bottom bar mein **Account** tab kholein, phir sheet ke neeche **Delete account** dabayein.
- Confirm karne ke liye apna **password** daalein.

Isse aapka account, financial profile, goals aur saare purchase decisions **hamesha ke liye delete** ho jate hain, aur ye **wapas nahi ho sakta**. Sirf sign out karna ho to **Logout** use karein.
next: How do I delete one decision?

entries.a:
To **delete a single decision**, open **My Decisions** and either:
- tap the **bin icon** next to the date on its row, or
- open the decision and press **Delete this decision**.

You will be asked to confirm. It removes only that analysis from your history, and it **cannot be undone**. Your account and other decisions are not affected.
entries.hi:
**Ek decision delete** karne ke liye **My Decisions** kholein aur:
- uski row par date ke paas wala **bin icon** dabayein, ya
- decision kholkar **Delete this decision** dabayein.

Confirm karna hoga. Isse sirf wahi analysis history se hatta hai aur ye **wapas nahi ho sakta**. Aapka account aur baaki decisions safe rehte hain.
next: How do I delete my account?

k: how do i add a goal
how do i create a goal
entries.a:
To add a goal, open the **Goals** page and use the **Create Goal** card at the top:
- **Goal name** (for example Emergency fund, Laptop, Trip)
- **Target amount** in ₹
- **Saved** so far (can be 0)
- **Target date**
- **Priority:** High, Medium or Low

Then tap **Save Goal**. It appears as a card with a progress bar, and Worthwise uses it when checking your purchases.
entries.hi: Goal add karne ke liye **Goals** page kholein aur upar wale **Create Goal** card mein bharein: **goal ka naam**, **target amount** (₹), ab tak **saved** (0 bhi chalega), **target date** aur **priority** (High, Medium ya Low). Phir **Save Goal** dabayein. Goal progress bar ke saath dikhega aur purchases check karte waqt Worthwise use dhyan mein rakhega.

entries.a:
Your **emergency fund** is money you keep aside for unexpected needs.
- It is **part of your total savings**, so nothing is deducted from your savings when you enter it.
- Worthwise treats it as **protected money** and warns you when a purchase would eat into it.
- It cannot be more than your total savings.
- It counts for up to **35 points** of your Financial Health score.

You set it on the **Financial Profile** page under Savings.
entries.hi:
**Emergency fund** wo paisa hai jo aap achanak aane wale kharchon ke liye alag rakhte hain.
- Ye aapki **total savings ka hi hissa** hai, isliye daalne par savings se kuch kat'ta nahi.
- Worthwise ise **protected money** maanta hai, aur agar koi purchase isme haath lagaye to aapko warning deta hai.
- Ye total savings se zyada nahi ho sakta.
- Financial Health score mein iske **35 points tak** milte hain.

Ise **Financial Profile** page par Savings mein set karein.
next: How is the financial health score calculated?
What goes in my financial profile?

entries.a:
Every verdict has its reasons on the result page, under **Why we recommend...**. Usually it comes down to:
- your **monthly surplus** (income minus expenses and EMIs)
- your **savings buffer** and emergency fund after the purchase
- how many **months** it would delay your goal

To move from WAIT or SKIP toward BUY: wait and save the surplus, find a **lower price** or a cheaper option, choose **EMI** with a small monthly amount, or improve your numbers on the Financial Profile page. Then use **Re-evaluate** on the saved decision to see the new result.
entries.hi:
Har verdict ki wajah result page par **Why we recommend...** mein likhi hoti hai. Aam taur par ye teen cheezein dekhi jati hain:
- aapka **monthly surplus** (income minus kharche aur EMI)
- purchase ke baad aapka **savings buffer** aur emergency fund
- goal kitne **mahine** peeche jayega

WAIT ya SKIP se BUY ki taraf jaane ke liye: ruk kar surplus bachayein, **kam price** ya sasta option dhundhein, chhoti **EMI** chunein, ya Financial Profile mein apne numbers update karein. Phir saved decision par **Re-evaluate** dabayein.

entries.a:
The **AI take** on the result page is a short, friendly explanation of your verdict, written for your specific numbers. It appears with a typing effect.

AI explanations are **limited each month**. If you have used them all, Worthwise shows its **standard explanation** instead. The decision itself is calculated in exactly the same way either way, and the limit resets next month.
entries.hi:
Result page par **AI take** aapke verdict ka chhota, saral explanation hota hai jo aapke apne numbers par based hota hai. Ye typing effect ke saath dikhta hai.

AI explanations ki **monthly limit** hoti hai. Sab use ho jayein to Worthwise uski jagah **standard explanation** dikhata hai. Decision dono hi case mein ek jaise calculate hota hai, aur limit agle mahine reset ho jati hai.

entries.a:
**Worthwise** is a personal purchase decision engine. Its motto is "Think before you spend."

Before you buy something, Worthwise weighs it against your income, expenses, savings, existing EMIs and goals, then gives a clear, explainable verdict: **BUY**, **WAIT** or **SKIP**.

It is not a spreadsheet or a general chatbot. It is a structured workspace that walks you through five questions: Can I afford it? What will it change? What is the impact on my goals? What if I wait? What should I do?
entries.hi:
**Worthwise** ek personal purchase decision engine hai. Kuch kharidne se pehle ye aapki income, kharche, savings, EMI aur goals ke saath check karta hai, aur saaf verdict deta hai: **BUY**, **WAIT** ya **SKIP**.

Ye paanch sawaalon par chalta hai: Kya main afford kar sakta hoon? Isse kya badlega? Goals par kya asar? Agar ruk jaun to? Mujhe kya karna chahiye?

entries.a:
Worthwise follows a simple flow:
- **Product details:** you enter what you want to buy and its price.
- **Personal context:** it reuses your saved financial profile (income, expenses, savings, EMIs, preferences). You do not re-enter anything.
- **Decision:** it checks affordability, goal impact and timing, then shows a verdict with reasons and a plan.

Your profile and goals are the foundation, so the more accurate they are, the sharper the advice.
next: What do BUY, WAIT and SKIP mean?

entries.a:
Quick start:
- **1.** Create an account (or tap **Try Demo** to look around with no signup).
- **2.** Fill in your **Financial Profile**: income, expenses, savings and emergency fund.
- **3.** Add a **Goal** you are saving toward.
- **4.** Open **Analyze Purchase**, enter what you want to buy, and get your verdict.

Setting up your profile once is enough. Every analysis after that is quick.
entries.hi:
Shuru karne ke steps:
- **1.** Account banayein (ya bina signup ke **Try Demo** dabayein).
- **2.** **Financial Profile** bharein: income, kharche, savings, emergency fund.
- **3.** Ek **Goal** add karein.
- **4.** **Analyze Purchase** kholein, jo kharidna hai wo daalein, aur verdict paayein.
next: What goes in my financial profile?

entries.a:
Every analysis ends with one of three verdicts:
- ✅ **BUY:** the purchase fits your cash flow and does not hurt your goals or emergency buffer in a meaningful way.
- ⏳ **WAIT:** it is affordable later, not comfortably now. You also get a recommended wait time and a safe price range for your budget.
- ❌ **SKIP:** it would strain your finances or push your goals back too far.

Sometimes the result suggests a better alternative instead. Each verdict comes with the reasons behind it.
entries.hi:
Har analysis ka ek verdict hota hai:
- ✅ **BUY:** purchase aapke cash flow mein fit hai aur goals ya emergency buffer ko zyada nuksaan nahi karta.
- ⏳ **WAIT:** abhi comfortable nahi, baad mein affordable. Saath mein wait time aur safe price range milti hai.
- ❌ **SKIP:** isse aapki finances par dabaav padega ya goals bahut peeche chale jayenge.
next: What is on the results page?

entries.a:
Affordability in Worthwise goes beyond "is the money in my account today?" It checks:
- your **cash flow** (income minus expenses, i.e. monthly surplus)
- your **savings buffer** and emergency fund
- your **existing EMIs** and any EMI the new purchase adds

That is why a purchase can look affordable on paper and still get a WAIT.
next: How is the financial health score calculated?

entries.a:
Worthwise shows exactly how a purchase shifts your goals, in **months**, not vague warnings.

The **Financial Impact** card compares two columns, *without purchase* and *with purchase*, for:
- your savings
- your monthly surplus
- your goal completion date

If a purchase pushes your goal date back, you will see the new date. Waiting a few months and saving the surplus usually removes most of the impact.
next: How do I add a goal?

entries.a:
To analyze a purchase, open **Analyze Purchase** and fill in step 1:
- **Product name** (e.g. headphones, course, phone)
- **Category:** Electronics, Home & Furniture, Fashion, Health & Fitness, Travel, Education or Other
- **Price** in ₹
- **Purchase type:** One-time or EMI
- **Why do you want this?** (a sentence or two helps)
- **Product URL** (optional, meant for auto-filling price and specs later)

Step 2 shows the financial profile Worthwise will use. Tap **Analyze Purchase** and you get your decision.
entries.hi: Purchase analyze karne ke liye **Analyze Purchase** kholein aur step 1 bharein: product name, category, price (₹), purchase type (One-time ya EMI), aur kyun chahiye. Product URL optional hai. Step 2 mein aapki financial profile dikhti hai, phir **Analyze Purchase** dabayein.
next: What is on the results page?

entries.a:
Choose **EMI** as the purchase type and three extra fields appear:
- **Down payment** (enter 0 if none)
- **Monthly EMI** in ₹
- **EMI duration** in months

Worthwise then shows the **total cost** of the purchase, and uses the EMI to work out how your monthly surplus changes. With **One-time**, the full price is treated as paid upfront.
next: What goes in my financial profile?

entries.a:
Your result page has these sections:
- **Verdict** with a score dial
- **Why we recommend...:** the reasons behind it, plus an AI explanation
- **Financial Impact:** with vs. without the purchase
- **Better Options** and **Market Research** (cheaper or similar products)
- **Future Affordability:** when it becomes comfortable
- **Your Purchase Plan:** concrete steps, with buttons **Save Purchase Plan**, **Done this purchase** and **Analyze Another Purchase**

**Future Affordability** shows how the picture changes over time, based on your current savings rate. It answers "What if I wait?"

For a WAIT verdict you also get a **recommended wait time** and a **safe price range** that fits your budget. Waiting a few months while saving your surplus, or finding the item at a lower price, can turn a WAIT into a BUY.
next: What do BUY, WAIT and SKIP mean?

entries.a: **Better Options** suggests alternatives that suit your budget better than the original purchase, and shows how much you would save by choosing one. It sits on the result page next to **Market Research**.
next: What is on the results page?

entries.a:
**Market Research** looks up real products online and groups them as:
- **Around your entered price**
- **Cheaper options**

Each card has a **View product** button that opens the retailer page. Live search counts toward your monthly search limit. If you have used all of it, market research pauses until the limit resets, but your decision and affordability numbers are not affected.

Your **purchase decisions are always calculated**, with no limit. Only two things are limited each month:
- the **AI explanation**
- the **live product search** (Market Research)

The dashboard card **API Usage This Month** shows how many you have used and how many remain, along with the date they reset. When a limit is reached the rest of the analysis still works normally.

Your **Financial Health** score is out of 100 and combines three things:
- **Savings rate** (up to 55 points)
- **Emergency fund progress** toward your target (up to 35 points)
- **A non-negative monthly surplus** (10 points)

Labels: **Good** (75 and above), **Needs attention** (45 to 74), **At risk** (below 45). If no income is saved yet it shows **Set up profile**.

To raise it: increase your surplus, build your emergency fund, and keep expenses below income.
next: What goes in my financial profile?

entries.a:
The **Overview** dashboard shows:
- a **financial snapshot** (income, expenses, savings, surplus, with helpful indicators)
- **Financial Health** score and metrics (savings rate, surplus, debt burden, emergency buffer)
- your top **goal** progress
- **API Usage This Month**
- **Recent Decisions** and **Planned Purchases**

There is also an **Analyze a Purchase** button at the top.
next: How is the financial health score calculated?

entries.a:
**My Decisions** stores every purchase you have analyzed so you can revisit the reasoning later.
- Filter by **All, Buy, Wait or Skip**
- **Search** by product name
- Tap any row to open the details: **Why this decision** and the **Action plan**
- From there you can **Re-evaluate**, mark **Done this purchase**, or delete the decision

**Re-evaluate** re-runs a saved decision using your **current** profile. Use it after your income, savings or goals change, for example when a WAIT might have become a BUY. You find it in the decision's detail view.
next: How do I update my profile?

entries.a: **Done this purchase** tells Worthwise you actually bought the item. It updates your **savings and monthly surplus** in your profile, so your financial health and all future analyses reflect the real numbers. You will find the button on the result page and in a decision's details.
next: How is the financial health score calculated?

entries.a: **Planned Purchases** lists the items you decided to wait on, with a progress bar showing how close you are to affording them. It appears on the dashboard under "Saving toward these already". Use **Save Purchase Plan** on a result to track it there.

On the **Goals** page you set what you are saving toward. Each goal has:
- a **name**
- a **target amount** (₹)
- how much you have **saved** so far
- a **target date**
- a **priority:** High, Medium or Low

Worthwise checks every purchase against your goals before recommending BUY, and your top-priority goal is shown on the dashboard.

Your **Financial Profile** powers every affordability check. It has:
- **Income:** monthly take-home
- **Expenses:** a monthly breakdown (housing, food, transport, subscriptions, other)
- **Savings:** your total, including the emergency fund
- **Emergency fund:** treated as protected money, with a warning if a purchase would eat into it
- **Preferences** and **Settings**

Press **Save Changes** to store edits (or **Discard** to undo). Values cannot be negative, and expenses higher than income are not accepted.
entries.hi: **Financial Profile** mein ye cheezein hoti hain: **Income** (monthly take-home), **Expenses** (housing, food, transport, subscriptions, other), **Savings** (emergency fund samet) aur **Emergency fund**. Badlav ke baad **Save Changes** dabayein. Values negative nahi ho sakti, aur expenses income se zyada nahi ho sakte.
next: How is the financial health score calculated?

entries.a:
In the profile, **Preferences** tune how conservative Worthwise is:
- **Risk tolerance:** Low, Moderate or High
- **Saving priority:** Goal-first, Balanced or Flexible
- **Purchase preference:** Value over brand, Quality-first or Balanced

A lower risk tolerance and a goal-first priority make recommendations more cautious.
next: What goes in my financial profile?

entries.a: The **Settings** card (at the bottom of the Financial Profile page) shows your account preferences: email notifications for new analyses, the weekly financial health summary, and the currency, which is **INR (₹)**. Worthwise currently works in Indian rupees only.

To create an account:
- **1.** Open **Get Started**, then the **Create account** tab.
- **2.** Enter your **name, gender, email** and a **password** (at least 8 characters).
- **3.** Tap **Send verification code**. A 6-digit code is emailed to you.
- **4.** Enter it and tap **Verify and create account**.

Did not get the code? Use **Resend code**, or **Change email** if you typed it wrong. Check your spam folder too.
entries.hi: Account banane ke liye: **Get Started** > **Create account** tab > naam, gender, email aur password (kam se kam 8 characters) daalein > **Send verification code** dabayein > email mein aaya 6-digit code daalein > **Verify and create account**. Code na aaye to **Resend code** ya **Change email** use karein, aur spam folder bhi dekhein.

entries.a:
Use the **Login** tab on the account page with your email and password. If you are sent back to the login screen, your session has probably expired, so just sign in again.

I cannot see or reset passwords. If you are stuck, you can always use **Try Demo** to explore without an account.

**Try Demo** opens a ready-made demo account, with no signup and no email needed. It is the quickest way to see a full analysis, the dashboard, goals and decisions. You will find the button on the landing page and on both the Login and Create account tabs. The demo gives you **2 analyses**; after that, create a free account with your real email to keep going.

entries.a: On desktop, use the **Logout** and **Delete account** buttons at the bottom of the left sidebar (on mobile, open your profile from the bottom bar). **Delete account** asks you to confirm with your password before anything is removed, so please be sure before you proceed.

Use the **sun / moon button** to switch between dark and light mode. It sits in the top bar of the landing page and in the app. Your choice is remembered on this device, so there is no flash of the wrong theme when you return.

Worthwise works in any modern browser on desktop, tablet and phone. On desktop you navigate with the left sidebar (Overview, Analyze Purchase, My Decisions, Goals, Financial Profile, Settings). On mobile the sidebar becomes a **bottom bar** with Overview, Analyze, Decisions and Goals. There is no separate app to install.

Your profile, goals and decisions are stored **under your own account** and you must sign in to see them. Deleting your account is available from the sidebar and needs your password.

I do not have details about the server's security setup, so for anything formal please check with the Worthwise team. Please avoid typing passwords or card numbers into this chat.

Worthwise is currently a **prototype build**, and I do not have any pricing information. The only limits I know of are the monthly caps on AI explanations and live product searches, which you can see on your dashboard.

When you open Worthwise you may see **"Waking up Worthwise"** for a few seconds. The server goes to sleep when nobody is using it and needs a moment to start, mostly the first time you visit. It usually clears up by itself within about 20 to 30 seconds. If it still hangs, refresh the page.

Sorry you hit a problem. Try these in order:
- Refresh the page and wait for "Waking up Worthwise" to finish.
- If you were sent to the login screen, sign in again.
- Check that income, savings and expenses are not negative, and that expenses are not higher than income.
- If an analysis shows no market research, your monthly search limit may be used up (the rest still works).

Tell me exactly what you see and I will help narrow it down.

Worthwise helps you reason about **purchases** using your own numbers. It is a decision aid, not professional financial, tax or investment advice, and it does not recommend investments. The result is only as accurate as the profile and goals you enter, so keep them up to date, and for big financial decisions consider talking to a qualified advisor.

Worthwise is a **prototype build**: a single-page web app (HTML, CSS and JavaScript) talking to a hosted backend. It was built by **Mr. Chetan**. I do not have contact details to share, so for feedback please reach out to whoever shared this app with you.

I can explain anything about Worthwise:
- how analysis works and what **BUY / WAIT / SKIP** mean
- EMI, goals, profile fields and preferences
- the dashboard, decisions, planned purchases and usage limits
- accounts, demo mode, themes and troubleshooting

When you are logged in you can also ask about **your own numbers**, for example "my financial health", "my savings" or "my goals".
next: How is the financial health score calculated?

entries.a: I'm the **Worthwise Assistant**, the built-in help bot for this app. I answer questions about how Worthwise works, and if you are logged in I can read your own profile and goals to answer "my..." questions.
